findings.reason: Reviewed, not a leak. Deletes only the caller's own rows: the where clause is always (userId, scopeType, scopeId) with userId taken from the session, so another tenant's data is never read or written, and a foreign id answers {"cleared":0} exactly like an unknown one. It deliberately takes no org context so a stale override still clears after its project or org is gone.

Reviewed, not a leak. In the replay the scope type is `org`, so this is a member saving their own notification preference for the org they belong to (requireOrgMember on organizationId; other orgs answer 404). Project, app, database and job scopes additionally need view access to the owning project (UserNotificationsService.resolveVisibleScope), so a project the caller cannot see answers like a missing one; see test/notification-scope-visibility.test.ts.
